column5: You are in a city park on a quiet morning.
You don't feel it, but you are flying east at a thousand kilometres an hour.
All of it, moving with the planet.
A wind of one thousand kilometres an hour hits the city.
The fastest gust ever measured on Earth was four hundred and eight.
Everything not part of the rock is gone.
Giant waves roll over the coasts.
Then the seas slowly drain toward the poles, and a belt of new land rises around the equator.
The Sun stops in the sky.
One day now lasts a whole year.
Every century, the day gets about two milliseconds longer.
Four hundred million years ago, a year had about four hundred days.
And on Venus, one day already lasts longer than its whole year.
That quiet morning is moving at a thousand kilometres an hour.
